title: Hosted source computation and space bound
statement: Let $M$ be a finite-state Boolean Turing machine with $k$ work tapes, let $y$ be a Boolean word, let $b$ be a Boolean value, and let $B\in\mathbb{N}$. Suppose the cleaned machine associated with $M$, started in its prescribed initialization state on input $y$, halts with output consisting of the single symbol $b$, leaves every work-tape cell blank and every work-tape head at position $0$, and keeps every work-tape head within distance $B$ of $0$ at every step up to halting. Then, from the hosted machine's initial configuration on $y$ with any valid input-head position among the $|y|+2$ positions, the hosted machine reaches a configuration with no state and output $[b]$ in finitely many steps; at every step up to and including that time, each work-tape head remains within distance $B$ of $0$.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet
the cleaned machine started in its initialization state on $y$ halts with output $[b]$
at the cleaned machine's halting time, all work-tape cells are blank
at the cleaned machine's halting time, all work-tape heads are at position $0$
throughout the cleaned run up to halting, every work-tape head has absolute position at most $B$
the hosted run starts with any position in $\mathrm{Fin}(|y|+2)$ for its input head
